name: Aerospace Wire & Cable Inc
old_description: Specialized Manufacturers of High-Performance Custom High-Temperature Wire & Cable Solutions
about:
Aerospace Wire & Cable Inc. was founded in 1986 in Flushing, New York. The company operates as a specialized manufacturer of high-performance custom high-temperature wire and cable solutions.

The company produces a range of wire and cable products including communication, signal, coaxial, data and low-capacitance cables, fire alarm cables, instrumentation and tray cable, thermocouple cable, RTD cable, and hook-up wire. Manufacturing processes cover extrusion through jacketing, with custom design supported by a cable worksheet. The product line spans AWG sizes from 4/0 through 30, with insulation options such as FEP, foamed FEP, ETFE, PFA, PTFE, Kapton, LS-PVC, ECTFE, PEEK, and ECA 3000. Rated voltages reach up to 1,000 volts and operating temperatures from -80°C to +300°C. The firm also maintains an inventory of UL-listed types Z, ZW, and PFAH.

Aerospace Wire & Cable serves the aerospace, appliance, fire alarm, instrumentation, and industrial sectors. Its UL AWM listings support appliance wiring applications, while its high-temperature cables are used in aerospace and industrial environments. The company also supplies standard and special designs for communication, signal, and data transmission needs.

The business emphasizes custom high-temperature cable design, a broad insulation material portfolio, and UL-listed product availability as key differentiators. It was established to provide specialized wire and cable solutions for demanding thermal and electrical requirements.

about:
Agility Engineering & Manufacturing Solutions, based in St. Paul, Minnesota, traces its roots to 1952. The company operates as a 100% employee-owned organization, a structure that aligns incentives across its workforce and reinforces a culture of accountability. While the founders are not named in public records, the business has maintained continuous operation for over seven decades, evolving from a component supplier into a full-spectrum electromechanical partner.

The firm provides distribution, custom manufacturing, and engineering services for electromechanical components. Its capabilities span supply chain management, component repackaging (certified under CSA 238922 and UL TEOU2), wire harness assembly (UL ZPFW2), and UL 508 control panel fabrication (UL NITW7). Engineering support covers the product life cycle from design consultation through end-of-life management, allowing customers to consolidate vendors for both off-the-shelf and custom-built assemblies.

Agility serves original equipment manufacturers in agriculture, medical devices, and IoT infrastructure. Examples include mobility controls for farm machinery, sensing equipment for hospital-grade instruments, and assemblies that support connected IoT networks. The customer base ranges from industrial OEMs to specialized medical equipment makers who require certified components and responsive engineering collaboration.

The company emphasizes its HEART values — Honest communication, Evolution through innovation, Accountability, Respect, and Teamwork — as the foundation of client relationships. It differentiates itself through employee ownership, which it says drives flexibility and speed, and through the ability to deliver both distribution and custom solutions under one roof, reducing lead times and coordination overhead.

name: Akrion Technologies
old_description: Our legacy of over 30 years in the semiconductor industry is built on delivering cutting-edge wet process technologies that drive your success. Discover how our expertise can transform your operations.
about:
Akrion Technologies is based in Allentown, Pennsylvania, and has spent over 30 years developing wet process equipment for the semiconductor industry. The company was established to provide customized wafer surface preparation solutions, though the exact founding year and original founders are not publicly disclosed.

The company designs and builds automated wet stations for cleaning and stripping wafers ranging from 100 mm to 300 mm in diameter. Its product lines include the GAMA fully automated wet station, the PINNACLE SERIES cassetteless wet stations, and the V3 compact wet station, each handling batch sizes of 25 or 50 wafers. Akrion also supplies CVD, etch, furnace, and off‑line process tools, and reports more than 300 systems delivered to over 100 customers across five global locations.

Akrion serves the microelectronics sector, targeting analog IC, digital IC, power IC, MEMS, and R&D markets. Its equipment processes substrates such as silicon, silicon carbide, glass, and sapphire, supporting both bare and patterned wafers in production and research environments.

The company emphasizes customizable modular platforms, 24‑hour phone support for emergency service, and disciplined process management that it says reduces installation times and delivers high product reliability. Full technical support — including installation, maintenance, process assistance, training, parts repair, and system upgrades — rounds out its offering.
